elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor in an acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free successor carve-out expressly covers an acquisition.

result.reason: The redline satisfies every preferred requirement but fails the fallback's mutual consent-free successor-assignment right because Licensor receives no such carve-out or notice mechanism. It is not minimal: it additionally requires Licensee notice, covers consolidation, reorganization, and equity sales, adds a no-delay standard, and bars suspension, repricing, and modification after a Change of Control. Drafting quality is materially impaired because the retained sentence declaring any Licensee assignment without consent void facially conflicts with the new consent-free assignment carve-outs; it should be limited to assignments made in violation of the section. That introduced inconsistency also prevents a finding that the redline fully preserves intent.
